description:
The vocabulary a repository needs to be usable is declared in a package an adopter applies, and a repository that applies none receives none.

## Background

A fresh repository today receives a four-level type hierarchy, seven label namespaces, six item kinds, validation defaults and a documentation-area classification, none of which it declared and all of which are rendered from a compiled template. A repository that declares no registry at all receives one anyway, from default implementations reached through fallback branches — so even an adopter who writes their own configuration cannot decline the engine's.

Both routes close here. The compiled defaults go, so a repository receives what it declared and nothing else. The vocabulary itself becomes a package, and the workflow package declares a dependency on it rather than restating it. Both packages then ride in the release archive, so obtaining them costs no second download.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A repository declaring no namespaces and no type hierarchy receives neither, and still validates.
- [hard] REQ-02: A package declares the generic vocabulary a repository needs to be usable, carrying no workflow content.
- [hard] REQ-03: The workflow package declares a dependency on it and only the vocabulary it adds.
- [hard] REQ-04: The release archive carries both package directories, and the release smoke path applies the workflow package from the extracted archive.
- [hard] REQ-05: The suite's assertions about type names rest on a fixture that declares its own taxonomy rather than on any shipped default.

## Notes

The compiled template that renders today's configuration is deleted by the work that can prove these packages replace it.
title: The generic domain vocabulary reaches a repository as a package
